sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 893 of 2023

Applicant :- Shyam Singh @ Pappu
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashutosh Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kuldeep Singh Chahar
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
Heard Sri Ashutosh Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Kuldeep Singh Chahar, learned
counsel for the informant and Sri Tanay Kumar, learned Aga, for the State.
The instant bail application has been moved on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release
him on bail in Case Crime No.125 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 406, 504, 506, 452
and 323 Ipc, Police Station Manth, District Mathura during pendency of the trial.

Fir of the present case was lodged against the applicant and four others and according to the Fir,
applicant and other co-accused persons under the false promise to provide government job to the
informant received Rs.12,00,000/- from the informant and thereafter informant received forged
joining letter and in spite of repeated request his money was also not returned by the accused
persons and thus applicant and other co-accused persons mis-appropriated Rs.12,00,000/- of the
informant.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation against the applicant is totally false and baseless and applicant neither received any money nor he ever promised to the informant that he will provide him government job.

He next submits that applicant actually give some loan to the Shyam Singh @ Pappu vs State Of U.P. on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177013808/
1 informant on interest basis but in spite of repeated request made by applicant, his money was not returned by the informant and only due to this reason applicant has falsely been implicated by the informant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that although during investigation Investigating Officer also recorded the statements of number of villagers including the panch witnesses and they also stated that applicant admitted that he received total Rs.12,00,000/- from the informant and he assured that money will be returned to him but their statements cannot be believed as from the perusal of statement it appears that these statements are verbatim the same and no reliance can be placed on such version.
He next submits that there is no evidence on record except bald allegation that applicant and others received Rs.12,00,000/- from the informant.
He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history to his credit and he is in jail since 1.11.2022.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant along with others duped the informant and received total Rs.12,00,000/-
from him under the pretext to provide him government job but neither informant got the job nor his money was returned.

Learned for the informant further submits that during investigation Investigating Officer recorded the statements of number of villagers including the statements of panch witnesses before whom panchayat was held and from the perusal of their statements it appears that in the Panchayat applicant admitted that he received total Rs.12,00,000/- from the informant and he assured that his money will be returned.
This fact clearly suggests that applicant received total Rs.12,00,000/- from the informant and, therefore, the defence taken by applicant appears to be prima facie false.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

Although in the FIR it is mentioned that total Rs.12,00,000/- in cash was given by the informant to the applicant and others for providing him government job and applicant in paragraph-13 to the affidavit filed in support of the present bail application denied this fact and stated that he did not receive the money but in the FIR it is also mentioned that panchayat was held in the village in this regard and in the panchayat applicant admitted that he received total Rs.12,00,000/- from the informant and he also stated that he will return the money and this fact is evident from the statements of panch witnesses which were recorded by Investigating Officer during investigation.

As there is evidence on record which can show that applicant received total Rs.12,00,000/- from the informant under the pretext to provide him government job, therefore, prima facie it appears that the defence taken by applicant is false.
Therefore, considering the totality of the circumstances, in my view, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
